title: Managing a legacy Feed-in Tariff installation
subtitle: Meter readings, payment records, and what happens when you sell a house with a FiT
excerpt: The Feed-in Tariff (FiT) scheme closed to new applicants in 2019 but continues to pay existing participants for the duration of their 20-year contract. Understanding what readings to submit, how the export payment is calculated, and what happens at a property sale prevents payment interruptions and protects the financial return.
sourceNotes: Ofgem Feed-in Tariff guidance for participants (published and maintained on Ofgem website). BEIS FiT review 2018 confirming scheme closure timeline. Ofgem FiT register public data. HMRC guidance on FiT income and tax treatment for residential properties.

glossaryTerms.definition: The FiT payment per kWh of electricity generated by the installation, paid regardless of whether the electricity is used on-site or exported. The rate was fixed at the point of joining the scheme.
Under the FiT scheme, a payment for electricity exported to the grid. Most residential FiT participants receive a deemed export payment of 50% of generation (not metered directly).

content.text: The Feed-in Tariff runs for 20 years from the installation date. For systems installed between 2010 and 2012 (the peak of solar uptake), contracts expire between 2030 and 2032. Payments are made by the FiT licensee (electricity supplier) and require a meter reading submission, typically quarterly. Missing a submission quarter does not lose the payment permanently but does delay it until the next submission.
The generation meter records the total electricity the panels have produced. Most FiT participants read it quarterly and submit the reading.

Keep a spreadsheet log of quarterly readings with dates. This protects against disputes if the meter is replaced or readings are queried by the licensee.
The FiT contract is transferable to a new owner. The seller must notify the FiT licensee of the change of ownership and provide the completion date and buyer's details.
Give the buyer the MCS certificate, the FiT registration number, and the meter serial number. Also provide 12 months of reading history and the FiT licensee's contact details.
The FiT payment continues on the same tariff rate for the remaining contract term after the transfer. The buyer takes over the obligation to submit readings.
Payments are not automatically paused at sale. A final reading at the completion date splits the payment between seller and buyer for the quarter in which the sale falls.

HMRC confirmed in 2010 that FiT generation tariff income for owner-occupiers is not subject to income tax. This does not apply to landlords receiving FiT on rented property. The SEG export tariff is also tax-free for owner-occupiers under current HMRC guidance.

Once a FiT contract expires, the generation tariff and export tariff both cease. The panels continue to generate electricity and reduce bills through self-consumption. To continue receiving export payments, register for a SEG tariff with an eligible supplier. An SEG tariff can be set up independently of FiT; there is no requirement for FiT to have expired first.

rows.symptom: FiT payments have stopped without notification
rows.cause: The contract has been suspended pending meter reading submission, the licensee has changed (supplier switch), or the licensee has not processed the reading
rows.fix: Contact the FiT licensee directly with your FiT registration number and your most recent meter reading. If the licensee has changed due to a supplier switch, Ofgem can confirm the new licensee via their FiT register.
